recognize_zh: 骨髓切片中箭頭所指的血管壁被一層層無細胞、淡粉紅色、均質蠟樣的物質增厚，管腔變窄；這種血管壁無定形嗜酸性沉積就是類澱粉（amyloid），在類澱粉沉積症中可吸附第十凝血因子而造成後天性 factor X 缺乏。
features: Blood vessel with markedly thickened wall replaced by acellular, homogeneous, pale eosinophilic material (arrows)
Lamellated, waxy appearance of the deposit with narrowed lumen
Additional smaller vessel with similar hyaline wall deposition at the top
Adjacent bony trabecula and cellular marrow with maturing hematopoiesis and megakaryocytes
No obvious plasma cell sheets in this field
describe_en: Bone marrow core biopsy (H&E) shows a medium-sized blood vessel whose wall is markedly thickened and replaced by acellular, homogeneous, waxy pale eosinophilic material, with narrowing of the lumen; a second smaller vessel shows similar deposition. The adjacent marrow is cellular with maturing trilineage hematopoiesis, and no plasma cell sheets are seen in this field. Confirmation requires Congo red staining with apple-green birefringence under polarized light, and amyloid typing (e.g., mass spectrometry). Findings are suggestive of vascular amyloid deposition, consistent with systemic AL amyloidosis in the setting of acquired factor X deficiency.

ddx.vs: Seen in hypertension, diabetes, and aging, with homogeneous hyaline walls that are Congo red negative without apple-green birefringence.
Consists of pale extracellular mucopolysaccharide in the interstitium, Alcian blue positive and Congo red negative, rather than vessel wall deposits.
Deposits are Congo red negative and non-fibrillary, with granular deposits on electron microscopy.
Shows brightly eosinophilic fibrin with inflammatory cells and karyorrhexis in the wall, not bland lamellated deposits.
